mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering a sell-off in equities and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 during late-cycle expansions (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 360,000 million dollars indicates strong consumer spending, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS exceeds 360,000 million dollars (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 220.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal a deteriorating labor market, reducing household income and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) below 13200 billion dollars signals a slowing economy, reducing corporate earnings growth and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 < 13200 during late-cycle expansions (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).
